title: Spring 1 practice texts 'The Last Ferry' and 'Advice to Those Who Travel by Sea'
subject: English Language
source: Written for english-language/y11 lesson 41 (Spring 1 practice texts 'The Last Ferry' and 'Advice to Those Who Travel by Sea' (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 41: Mock repair: Q7 comparison and Section B ideas in your own words. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

head: Not this
This
rows: Text One feels scared. Text Two is calm. (Two separate paragraphs, no methods.)

Both writers present the sea as in control, although Text One's personal fear contrasts with Text Two's amused calm; the first-person memoir draws us into fear, whereas the imperatives of Text Two lecture the reader.

blocks.h: Section B: transform, do not lift

model.title: Compare how the writers present the experience of sea travel. (15 marks)

parts.text: P: both present the sea as powerful, although one fears it and one accepts it
M: personification in both; first person versus imperatives
A: fear draws us in; advice keeps us at a distance
C and S: travel teaches humility in both

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: An integrated paragraph with both texts, both ideas and methods, and a judgement.

keywords.def: a writer's viewpoint shaped by time and experience
change an idea into your own words and purpose
copy words from the text: loses AO1 marks

questions.q: Transform this text idea into advice for a Year 9 audience: 'the ordinary safety I had been so keen to escape'.
questions.a: For example: You may feel homesick on your first trip; that feeling shows how much home matters, and it passes.

questions.q: Write the P and E of a Q7 paragraph on the writers' attitudes to travel.
questions.a: P: both value what travel teaches, although... E: one short quotation from each text.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, rewrite your weakest mock Q7 or Q8 paragraph using today's models. Starter (Q7): 'Both writers present..., although...' or (Q8): 'If you are...'
questions.a: A repaired paragraph: integrated comparison with methods (Q7), or transformed ideas for audience and purpose (Q8).

questions.q: Extend: highlight every comparative connective (Q7) or transformed idea (Q8).
Stretch: write a conclusion sentence that synthesises both texts.
questions.a: For example: Ultimately, both writers suggest that the sea teaches humility, though only one learns it through fear.

questions.q: Which Q8 sentence earns AO1 best?
options: The sea was the colour of wet slate.
You may face long delays, so pack patience as well as a book.
The ferry was forty minutes late.
questions.a: B) You may face long delays, so pack patience as well as a book.. It transforms an idea from the texts for the new audience; the others lift details.
A) both texts in every paragraph

questions.q: Answer the ponder in one sentence.
questions.a: Because AO1 in Section B rewards using ideas in your own words for a new purpose, not copying.
